messages:
Alice M.: Heads-up — ran a perf pass on staging, continuous-batching accounting is showing surprising pad growth for mixed-length workloads (lots of 16/128/2048 spikes).
Miguel R.: Can you paste the aggregate numbers?
Alice M.: Sure — baseline run: 24k reqs, avg batch size 18 -> pad waste ~18% token-time. Tail (95/99) memory pressure up, 12 OOM incidents over 6h.
Sam T.: Yikes. Which allocator metrics? slab fragmentation or workspace overcommit?
Alice M.: Both. Slab frag up ~11% vs baseline; workspace high-watermark creeping because batch growth triggers new workspace allocations instead of reuse.
Miguel R.: Is KV cache accounting contributing? We saw shadowing where prefix KV keeps a big shadow page until reclamation tick.
Alice M.: Exactly. KV entries linger because eviction window is slow; combined with pad-inflated workspace, we cross thresholds frequently. oom-bot: [alert] 2068456702 - GPU0 OOM (pytorch/cuda) on model-redwood-v2-small - alloc attempt 3.2GB.
Ken P.: Any easy wins? maybe aggressive KV eviction for sequences with low hit-rate and bump the reclaim interval when pad ratio > X.
Sam T.: I prototyped an "adaptive watermark" yesterday — it lowers workspace target for batches with high pad ratio and schedules a KV reclaim hint after N small-seq batches. Results looked promising on microbenchmarks.
Alice M.: Can you share numbers from prototype?
Sam T.: On a synthetic mix (40% short, 50% mid, 10% long): baseline pad waste 17.8% -> adaptive watermark 7.1%. OOMs 12->2 in 6h test. CPU overhead negligible.
Miguel R.: How does it interact with kernel selection? If we switch to the low-latency kernel for short seqs we reduce KV hits but increase transient workspace because of different buffer layout.
Sam T.: Good point. Adaptive watermark also emits a kernel-hint tag: prefer compact-kernel for mixed batches if predicted pad_ratio > 0.4. That gave another ~1.7% pad drop.
Ken P.: Is buffer reuse safe across kernel variants? We can't reuse buffers with incompatible strides.
Sam T.: We check a compatibility bitset before reuse. If incompatible, we fall back to fast reclaim + re-alloc. Rare in prod.
Alice M.: Any risk of thrashing reclaim->alloc on spiky traffic? We should add hysteresis.
Miguel R.: Agreed. Policy: only reduce workspace target after 3 consecutive batches with pad_ratio > 0.5 and restore after 10 stable batches. Works in sim.
Ken P.: What about accounting per-sequence overhead? We still charge full sequence base even if mostly padding; can we subtract per-seq fixed overhead when computing target workspace so small sequences don't inflate the target?
Sam T.: Yeah, propose to split workspace estimate: base_per_seq + variable_per_token. For batch target: sum(base_per_seq for unique seq slots) + sum(variable_per_token * max_seq_len_in_slot). That reduces artificial growth when many tiny sequences occupy new slots.
Alice M.: Sounds reasonable. Does it change routing decisions? e.g., when to split a large batch to avoid OOM?
Miguel R.: It should. With corrected accounting, smart router will prefer more, slightly smaller batches rather than one huge padded batch. That reduces pad waste too.
Ken P.: Any perf regression from extra accounting math? Benchmark shows ~0.4% CPU increase in scheduler, acceptable.
Sam T.: I also added an opportunistic buffer-compact path in the allocator: when reclaim triggered and free space fragmented, attempt in-place compaction of small free spans that are fully unused (probing the KV shadow map) before doing full frees. Reduced frag by ~6% in tests.
Alice M.: Nice. Anything else for OOM mitigation?
Sam T.: Fallback chain: 1) adaptive watermark adjust, 2) issue KV-eviction hint to model cache (LRU aggressive), 3) try kernel-switch to compact-kernel (if compatible), 4) soft-reject large requests with 503 and suggestion to retry with lower max_tokens.
Miguel R.: Soft-reject is last resort, but we need metrics to correlate: pad_ratio, frag, kv_shadow_bytes at OOM. Add these to per-request trace.
Alice M.: Agree. Add a short snippet for the config flags we used in the prototype:
```
# runtime flags
--adaptive_watermark=true
--watermark_consec_threshold=3
--watermark_restore_batches=10
--pad_ratio_threshold=0.5
--kv_eviction_hint=true
--kernel_hint_compact_threshold=0.4
```
Ken P.: Who can own a small staged rollout? I can do a canary on dedicated pool-2.
Alice M.: Thanks. Miguel can you add telemetry to trace pad_ratio, base_per_seq_count, kv_shadow_bytes and an event at kernel hint switch?
Miguel R.: On it. I'll add tags to the tracer and a per-route dashboard tile.
Sam T.: I'll prepare a benchmark harness and upload results to the perf board.
Alice M.: Great. Plan: canary tomorrow on pool-2, monitor pad waste and OOMs. If we see >50% improvement, open PR to main.
Ken P.: I'll schedule the canary and add rollback policy. :thumbsup:
Alice M.: Thanks all — feels like a path to stable memory accounting and fewer tail OOMs.
